Q: Filter out results only if match 2 cells on same line A:

Use ifna(), join() and filter(), like this:

=ifna(unique(join(", ", filter(
  'Sales DB'!C$2:C, 
  'Sales DB'!C$2:C <> B2, 
  'Sales DB'!D$2:D = C2,
  'Sales DB'!A$2:A = left(D2, len('Sales DB'!A$2:A))
))))

]

The unique() is only necessary if you want to remove possible duplicates.

Q: How to disable Next.js telemetry permanently in all environments? A:

What about to use CLI command to check and then disable TELEMETRY i next.js - you can use below commands:

npx next telemetry status - to see the status

npx next telemetry disable - to disable telemetry

npx next telemetry enable- to enable telemetry

Q: Native windows c++ programming? A:

In theory, the Exe file can run on any computer with suitable CPU etc.
(same opcode "language" as yours).

Practically, there are two major problems:

a) The program file contains more than CPU commands, what and how depends on eg, your operating system. Exe (PE) files are usually used in Windows, and while it is theoretically possible, Linux won´t run it because nobody programmed it in a way to understand Exe files (there is additional software like Wine, which can run Exe´s on Linux, but that has to be installed separately)

b) You´re not writing every bit from the OS from scratch, you´re relying that you can use a lot of pre-existing functions. As you know, these have to be present to run your program. The problem is, Visual Studio assumes the presence of libraries which are intentionally not part of Windows itself. It wouldn´t be a problem to ship them with every Windows installation, but Microsoft choose to keep them as separate download (the Redist. package mentioned in the comments). To stuff as much as possible in the Exe file without relying on other library files, use the static linking option for your project.

Q: What exactly does AI do beyond ML models and rule-based logic? A:

Not sure I can answer everything here, but let me see how I can help:

  1. The idea of AI systems is that it could be a interwoven pipeline of multiple models and steps.

    For example, imagine you want to classify texts in specific categories of your choosing. But to have supervised learning on it, you need all the data labeled with the categories you want. You don't want to go trough your millions of text snippets and label them. So, you can use unsupervised, like clustering, to separate your texts into piles of similar ones. Then you can label the clusters based on a limited number of samples that you actually read, and voila - you now have a labeled set for your supervised learning, with which you can continue. You just used two different ML models here, thus making it a system.

  2. That said, ML is a subset of AI - so all ML is AI, but not vice versa - even in your example you are talking about AI as ML+the rules. In that same manner LLMs, which we can consider AI, are the ML models used for NLP + the prompt engineering + the parameter tuning + ideally some decision making on reliability of the sources (like - don't use things you scrape from this list of websites, because they are not true) etc.

  3. On that point, decision making by AI can appear on any level - could be "don't use data based on this input", or "if the probability is higher than x, flag this", or "add this article to that cluster", or "ban this user", or "correct this text while it is being written" - they are all decisions, even if some have more real world impact than others. Decision making is a very broad term for "do something autonomously", where the something can be in any stage. Even a simple classification model that we use as a blackbox makes some decisions inside. (And that is why it is so hard to have those explainable - why did the ML model classify this input like that? And then it might be that you look into it, and it had 52%t certainty, and you absolutely should not have based a whole project on it.).

Q: AutocadLisp - let variable argument definition mistaken as e function A:

actually, AutoLISP is specialized language for CAD programs, so it is not compatible with CommonLISP in many ways.

the reason that the codes generated by AI are inaccurate is that there are relatively small autolisp codes, so the AI tries to use some codes of CommonLISP instead, which is not compatible with.
